Visualisation of frequency tables

count_data <- dt %>%
  group_by(event_type) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count)) %>%
  mutate(event_type = factor(event_type, levels = event_type))

ggplot(data = count_data, aes(x = event_type, y = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "pink") +
  labs(title = "Event Type Counts",
       x = "Type of event",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() + geom_text(aes(label=count), vjust=1.6, color="blue",
            position = position_dodge(0.9), size=3.5)

count_data <- dt %>%
  group_by(category_code) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(count)) %>%

inappropriate values

The variables category_code and brand have inappropriate values like “” which are empty. we will be segregating brand to 0 and 1 wth “” as 0 and rest as 1 . Similary for category_code we will be labelling as Unknown , appliances,accessories,furniture and stationery. it also has sport.diving label which we will add into unknown as it has only 2 values from the total data so create a dummy at the time of building a model wont make sense.

dt$category_code[dt$category_code == ""] <- "unknown"

merge_categories <- function(category) {
  if (grepl("^furniture", category))
    return("furniture")

  if (grepl("^appliances", category))
    return("appliances")
  
  if (grepl("^accessories", category))
    return("accessories")
  
  if (grepl("^sport", category))
    return("unknown")
  
  return(category)
}

dt$category_code <- sapply(dt$category_code, merge_categories)

dt$brand = ifelse(dt$brand == "",0,1)
table(dt$brand)
## 
##       0       1 
## 1659261 2443022

Oultier detection and removal

Q1 <- quantile(dt$price, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3 <- quantile(dt$price, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR <- Q3 - Q1

lower_bound <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
upper_bound <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

outliers <- dt[dt$price < lower_bound | dt$price > upper_bound, ]

dt_no_outliers <- dt[dt$price >= lower_bound & dt$price <= upper_bound, ]

### Brand type count visualisation after outlier removal

1 = Top known brands , 0 = local / unknown brands

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)

count_data <- dt_no_outliers %>%
  group_by(brand) %>%
  summarize(count = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(brand = as.factor(brand),  # Convert brand to a factor
         brand = fct_reorder(brand, count))  # Reorder brand by count

ggplot(data = count_data, aes(x = brand, y = count)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "grey") +
  labs(title = "Brand Type Counts",
       x = "Brand Type",
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), vjust = -0.3, color = "black", size = 3.5)

Creation of new variables for EDA

dt_no_outliers$event_time = ymd_hms(dt_no_outliers$event_time)
dt_no_outliers$day_of_week <- weekdays(dt_no_outliers$event_time)
dt_no_outliers$hour <- hour(dt_no_outliers$event_time)
dt_no_outliers$time_of_day <- cut(
  dt_no_outliers$hour,
  breaks = c(0, 12, 18, 24),
  labels = c("morning", "afternoon", "evening"),
  include.lowest = TRUE,
  right = FALSE
)

Here we are grouping our event type into 3 types: Morning Afternoon Evening

Dummy variables

library(fastDummies)
## Thank you for using fastDummies!

Finding the average price for dependent variable ( Yes / no)

Count of event type cart : dependent variable

table(dt$event_type_cart)
## 
##       0       1 
## 2499650 1164087

we can see that our data is unbalanced. its a unbalanced dataset. and before we proceed for anything we need to banlance it and for that we will be using ROSE to balance the target variable . The data generated from oversampling have expected amount of repeated observations. Data generated from undersampling is deprived of important information from the original data. This leads to inaccuracies in the resulting performance. To encounter these issues, ROSE helps us to generate data synthetically as well. The data generated using ROSE is considered to provide better estimate of original data.

dt1 = dt
dt1 = dt1 %>% select(c(category_code_accessories,category_code_apparel.glove,category_code_furniture,category_code_appliances,category_code_stationery.cartrige,category_code_unknown,brand,price,event_type_cart))
dt1 = dt1 %>% mutate_if(is.integer,as.factor)
dt1$brand = as.factor(dt1$brand)
library(pROC)
## Type 'citation("pROC")' for a citation.
## 
## Attaching package: 'pROC'
## The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     cov, smooth, var
library(caret)
## Loading required package: lattice
## 
## Attaching package: 'caret'
## The following object is masked from 'package:purrr':
## 
##     lift
library(ROSE)
## Loaded ROSE 0.0-4
set.seed(123)
index <- createDataPartition(dt1$event_type_cart, p = 0.6, list = FALSE)
train_data <- dt1[index, ]
test_data <- dt1[-index, ]

data.rose <- ROSE(event_type_cart ~ ., data = train_data, seed = 1)$data
table(data.rose$event_type_cart)
## 
##       0       1 
## 1099699 1098544

we can see that the data is balance for the number of people who have kept their items in cart and who have not 0 1 1099699 1098544

####Logestic regression

ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5, classProbs = FALSE)
model_glm <- train(event_type_cart ~ ., data = data.rose, method = "glm", trControl = ctrl)


predictions_glm <- predict(model_glm, newdata = test_data)

conf_matrix_glm <- confusionMatrix(predictions_glm, test_data$event_type_cart)
print(conf_matrix_glm)

Decision tree

library(rpart)
model_dt <- train(event_type_cart ~ ., data = data.rose, method = "rpart", trControl = ctrl)

predictions_dt <- predict(model_dt, newdata = test_data)

conf_matrix_dt <- confusionMatrix(predictions_dt, test_data$event_type_cart)
print(conf_matrix_dt)

Overall Comparison:

The decision tree model performs better in terms of overall accuracy, sensitivity, and detection rate.Both models exhibit a trade-off between sensitivity and specificity, emphasizing the importance of considering business objectives and the associated costs of false positives and false negatives.

Error Rates and Accuracy Rates:

error_rate_glm <- 1 - conf_matrix_glm$overall["Accuracy"]
error_rate_dt <- 1 - conf_matrix_dt$overall["Accuracy"]

accuracy_rate_glm <- conf_matrix_glm$overall["Accuracy"]
accuracy_rate_dt <- conf_matrix_dt$overall["Accuracy"]

cat("Logistic Regression Model Error Rate:", error_rate_glm, "\n")
## Logistic Regression Model Error Rate: 0.474902
cat("Decision Tree Model Error Rate:", error_rate_dt, "\n\n")
## Decision Tree Model Error Rate: 0.3797852
cat("Logistic Regression Model Accuracy Rate:", accuracy_rate_glm, "\n")
## Logistic Regression Model Accuracy Rate: 0.525098
cat("Decision Tree Model Accuracy Rate:", accuracy_rate_dt, "\n")
## Decision Tree Model Accuracy Rate: 0.6202148

Decile-wise Lift chart

library(gains)

predictions <- predict(model_glm, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
actuals <- test_data$event_type_cart

dt_lift <- data.frame(predictions = as.numeric(predictions), actuals = as.numeric(actuals))

dt_lift <- dt_lift[order(-dt_lift$predictions), ]

gains_table <- gains(predicted = dt_lift$predictions, actual = dt_lift$actuals)
## Warning in gains(predicted = dt_lift$predictions, actual = dt_lift$actuals):
## Warning: Fewer distinct predicted values than groups requested
barplot(gains_table$mean.resp / mean(dt_lift$actuals), names.arg = gains_table$depth, xlab = "Percentile", 
        ylab = "Mean Response", main = "Decile-wise lift chart")

predictions <- predict(model_dt, newdata = test_data, type = "raw")
actuals <- test_data$event_type_cart

dt_lift <- data.frame(predictions = as.numeric(predictions), actuals = as.numeric(actuals))

dt_lift <- dt_lift[order(-dt_lift$predictions), ]

gains_table <- gains(predicted = dt_lift$predictions, actual = dt_lift$actuals)
## Warning in gains(predicted = dt_lift$predictions, actual = dt_lift$actuals):
## Warning: Fewer distinct predicted values than groups requested
barplot(gains_table$mean.resp / mean(dt_lift$actuals), names.arg = gains_table$depth, xlab = "Percentile", 
        ylab = "Mean Response", main = "Decile-wise lift chart")

Lift curve

predictions <- predict(model_glm, newdata = test_data)


lift_data <- data.frame(
  actuals = as.factor(test_data$event_type_cart),
  predictions = as.numeric(predictions)
)

lift_curve_glm <- yardstick::lift_curve(data = lift_data,actuals,predictions)

autoplot(lift_curve_glm, main = "Lift Curve")

predictions <- predict(model_dt, newdata = test_data)


lift_data <- data.frame(
  actuals = as.factor(test_data$event_type_cart),
  predictions = as.numeric(predictions)
)

lift_curve_dt <- yardstick::lift_curve(data = lift_data,actuals,predictions)

autoplot(lift_curve_dt, main = "Lift Curve")

Comparison: Both models show an improvement in lift compared to the baseline. The decision tree model seems to have a higher lift at a lower percentage of data tested (37.33%) compared to the logistic regression model (53.24%).

Considerations: The lift curve helps you understand how well your model is performing compared to a baseline. Higher lift values indicate better performance.
